## Marker legend — the five provenance markers, and the fact that no script scores them

Every verdict cell is a backticked word with AT MOST ONE marker after it: `covered ᵗ`, `absent ʰ`,
`partial ᵏ`. The definitions with their strength ordering are §"Cell vocabulary"; this block sits at
the top because the correction header below starts USING the markers eight hundred lines before that
section defines them.

| Marker | One line | Where it is DEFINED |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ʳ` | **driven** — a live arm on the packaged build whose report names the controls | `VERDICT_CELL` + `MARKERS` in `scripts/plan-status.py` (D1.85, 2026-09-17) |
| `ᵗ` | a tracker row / a landed commit is the evidence — the strongest this file has | `EVIDENCE_MARKERS` in `scripts/check-coverage-map.ts` |
| `ʰ` | a hand check made for that pass — a call site, a schema, a shipped binary's strings was read | same |
| `ᵏ` | a code probe only — the identifier is present, the behaviour is NOT proven | same |
| `ˢ` | propagated — this cell repeats a measurement made elsewhere; it is not itself one | `SCOPE_MARKER`, same file, where it means SCOPE rather than evidence |
| `ᵈ` | doc-only — the vendor page, with nothing in our tree or their binary observed | **nowhere: no script carries this one** |

**`ʳ` — driven, the sixth marker and now the strongest (D1.85, owner 2026-09-17, built by WI-e `79072790e`).** A `ʳ` cell means **a live arm on the packaged build whose report names the controls**. It outranks `ᵗ` for the reason this file exists to record: a tracker row proves a build LANDED, a driven arm with a control proves it BEHAVES, and until now the ledger could only say the second in prose. It AMENDS the controller's 2026-09-12 rule below rather than replacing it — a packaged controlled drive whose report names no control is still `ʰ`, `ᵏ` still never upgrades a cell, and the marker is earned by the REPORT, not by the rig. **The decision named the glyph `ᵈ`, and `ᵈ` was not free:** it is the doc-only marker and wore **32** cells the day this landed (Pi 5 · Claude 10 · Codex 17, `python3 scripts/plan-status.py`), against this legend's own *"Zero cells wear it"* — a 2026-09-09 reading, stale by 32 — so re-using it would have re-labelled the weakest evidence in the file as the strongest, in silence. Only the character moved. **It is also the first marker with a reader that can go red:** `scripts/plan-status.py` accepts it in `VERDICT_CELL` and counts it in the census, and two arms are pinned in `scripts/plan-status-marker-census.test.ts` — a `ʳ` cell counted as driven with its verdict word intact, and the bare ASCII `r` a keyboard produces instead warning by name and being censused as UNMARKED rather than as driven. The denominator twin stays marker-less: `check-denominator-twin.ts` refuses a marked verdict cell there, pinned in its own test, so this marker cannot leak into the file whose vocabulary is its own. First ten cells (applied with this paragraph, 2026-09-17): A16 pi/claude, A19 codex, A22 ×3, A57 claude, A76 ×3; the second pass and the enforcement arm are D1.196/D1.197 of the integrations plan.

**A packaged, controlled DRIVE is a hand measurement — `ʰ`; `ᵏ` never upgrades a cell** (controller 2026-09-12, after RL5): two rig-day lanes asked for `ᵏ` on live packaged drives with controls as if it were the strongest marker; it is the weakest (a probe whose behaviour is not proven). A live drive that confirms a tracker row's build keeps `ᵗ` with the drive in the Why; a live drive with no tracker row behind it is `ʰ`.


**Which script is the source of truth — measured 2026-09-09, and the answer is that neither of the two
touching these characters SCORES them.**

- `scripts/plan-status.py` is the only script that parses THIS file, and it checks the marker's SHAPE
  alone: `VERDICT_CELL` accepts a verdict word plus at most one marker from that five-character class
  preceded by a space, and warns *"verdict cell N is not a verdict"* otherwise. `verdict()` then
  strips the backticks and takes the leading word, so a marker moves no number this file quotes, and
  the script prints no marker line of its own. The `ʰ` · `ᵗ` · `ᵏ` · `ˢ` · `ᵈ` provenance lines in
  §Counts were counted for those passes by hand — the shape check entered that script only on
  2026-09-03 (`d73156922`), after those lines were written.
- `scripts/check-coverage-map.ts` DEFINES four of the five and enforces them, but over the two
  coverage maps (`MAP_PATH`, `CODEX_MAP_PATH`) and never over this file. Its `ˢ` is documented as
  scope — *the seam is host-level, so this cell repeats one measurement* — which is the narrower
  parent of the "propagated" sense used here.
- `ᵈ` has no reader anywhere: it is in no script's vocabulary, surviving only inside that character
  class and in the table above. Zero cells WORE it — re-counted 2026-09-09 over 632 rows × 3 runtime
  columns: ᵗ 276 · ʰ 1415 · ˢ 12 · ᵏ 5 · ᵈ 0 · unmarked 188. **Re-counted 2026-09-17 (WI-e, D1.85): 32 cells wear `ᵈ` (Pi 5 · Claude 10 · Codex 17), so that zero was a reading with a date — and it is why the driven marker took a free glyph, `ʳ`, instead of this one; since D1.85 `scripts/plan-status.py`'s `VERDICT_CELL` accepts `ᵈ` and the census counts it, though still no script SCORES it.**

**So a marker is a promise to the reader, not an input to any score, and nothing goes red when one is
wrong.** That is the reason to write it carefully, and the reason §"Cell vocabulary" ranks them.

# The capability ledger — one row per thing a user can do, three runtime columns

**Written 2026-08-28 on `feat/TCODE-000`, corrected the same day by P3.35, then r5, r8, x8, the
21-commit refresh (s2), the 100-commit refresh (A1, 2026-09-02), the wave-1 refresh (S0-5,
2026-09-03), the stage-2 refresh (S2-0, 2026-09-03) and the wave-2/3 refresh (S3-0,
2026-09-03). Read-only. No source was changed; no plan row was opened. Measurements of my
own are in §Corrections and are marked as mine — C1 and C2 from the build pass, C3-C6 from the
correction pass.**

**Last read of the tree: `29d69a4d1` → `b220c4467` (S3-0, 2026-09-03), 118 of 177 commits touching
`packages/`, `apps/` or `scripts/` — a FIXED window, chosen because seven code lanes were committing
while this pass ran and a moving HEAD would have made the reading unrepeatable.** The tree at
`b220c4467` is code-identical to the wave-4 base `16b34edb1`; the only commit between them adds the
wave-4 brief and touches no source, which is why a window ending one commit short of HEAD is still a
complete reading of the code. **The brief this lane was given said 104 code commits, which is
`plan-status.py`'s counter and not the pathspec's 118** — the floor, again. The S2-0 line it replaces
read `0bb813b11` → `6bb67c143`, 30 of 50 commits. The S0-5 line before that read `c88a1e848` →
`1c02fa3b3`, 34 commits. The A1 line it replaces read `3288b115c` → `ec765802b`, 100
commits; the s2 line before that, `9e0596f2e` → HEAD, 21 commits. **A caution about the age counter
this file leans on, measured over this same window:** `scripts/plan-status.py` counts *commits since
the ledger's own last commit whose subject does not start with `docs`*, and over
`c88a1e848..1c02fa3b3` that denominator is **28** against the pathspec's **34** — six `docs(...)`-titled
commits carried code, among them `fff7021c7`, which corrected a claim P2.462 had measured false, and
`583a95982`, which is a permissions row. The counter is a floor, not a count, and it also runs to
HEAD rather than to the window a refresh actually read. The stamp
`scripts/plan-status.py` prints is derived from this file's own last commit, so it is honest without
being maintained; this line exists for a reader who does not run the script. A coverage figure
without its age is the defect — lanes close defects, so an unrefreshed ledger always UNDERSTATES,
and an understated number is the one nobody challenges.

**What this merge actually had in front of it — stated first, because it bounds everything after
it.** Four readers were dispatched over the six committed artefacts. **Two extracts reached me
whole** — the claude sweep's (55 capability records, with its own evidence-strength note) and the
codex sweep's (28 records, **truncated mid-entry** at row 53). The other two did not arrive. I
closed the gap by reading the underlying artefacts directly rather than by inferring:
`docs/architecture/runtime-capability-gaps.md` in full (it supplies the four-reason vocabulary, the
Pi/Claude/Codex gap tables, the R11 switch-cost record and the measured env-propagation finding),
and the codex sweep triage's §0, §4.1, §4.2, §5, §6 and rows 64-67 to recover what the truncation
took. **Two consequences to hold onto:** the two coverage maps were read only for their marker
legend and their corrected cells, not row by row — so *"the map says X"* claims below are the
sweeps' readings of the maps, not mine; and the 429-row parity-closure plan was not read at all, so
**no row below carries a `PLANNED` reason sourced from that plan except the four the artefacts
named by number** (R7, R46, R50, C12).

**The input gap is CLOSED — P3.35, and closing it was the single most productive thing in this
file's history.** The 429-row plan has now been read: 435 tracker rows extracted, 294 closed and 129
open. **A closed row's NOTE is the richest source in the repository of what actually landed, and it
repeatedly disagrees with the row's own title** — `P2.313`'s title says half the configuration
surface is inert on Pi and its note says *"THE ROW'S STATED MECHANISM IS REFUTED"*; `P2.108`'s title
says isolation reaches only Pi and its note retires it as *no gap*. Reading titles would have
produced a **worse** file than reading nothing. What that pass moved is in the header, and every
row whose reason now cites a `P2.x`/`P3.x` number got it here.

**Two duplicates it exposed, both caused by this file not having read the plan**: the ledger's own
queue rows **P3.30** and **P3.34** duplicate work that already existed — P3.30 restates the open row
**P2.252** (*"codex cannot be told about the bundled corporate CA"*), and P3.34 restates a defect
**already closed** in `d144ce041`. The tracker also carries **two colliding row ids** (`P3.30` and
`P3.31` each appear twice, once closed and once open), which is a bookkeeping defect this file can
report but not fix.

---

## What this is

The owner's goal is *"give the user every capability of the claude and codex runtimes, and of Pi
built to Claude's contract, through one host that switches correctly between them."*

Everything we had swept by **documentation page**. A page covers several capabilities and a
capability spans pages, so *"N pages green"* has never translated into *"the user can do X"*. This
file is that translation: **one row per capability, phrased from the user's or operator's side,
with a verdict and a provenance marker per runtime**, plus the reason for each absence and whether
the capability survives a runtime switch.

## What this is NOT

- **Not a completeness claim.** It enumerates **631** capabilities — 107 distilled from the reader extracts and,
  since P3.35, from the parity plan and one committed measurement. The
  claude sweep alone carried 378 findings and the codex sweep 65 entries; both explicitly declare
  under-probed regions (the codex sweep's own words: *"Codex is under-probed throughout"*, plus 73
  ⛔ map rows never re-triaged and 81 "not our surface" verdicts never re-examined). A capability
  absent from this file is **unenumerated**, not covered.
- **Not behaviour-proven, with SIX exceptions now — the score is being raised, and the exceptions
  keep inverting the reading they replace.** The claude sweep's own close-out: *"Every one of the 378
  entries is at static-reading strength… Nothing here is behaviour-proven."* The codex sweep ran no
  live turn either. Every `ᵏ` and most `ʰ` cells below are still identifier-and-control-flow claims.
  The exceptions: **A5's codex cell and J11** (a rig that drove the pinned binary per arm with
  controls, `185172b05`); **A1's claude cell** (five arms, two controls, env scrubbed, classifier
  requests counted off our own loopback — `b0e6f0044` — plus 28 live gateway verdicts parsed by the
  binary's own parser in `6f3cc6443`); **A4's claude cell** (four calls in ONE run from ONE settings
  object against the vendored 2.1.223, with the `Read`-denial as the control that makes the three
  absences findings); and **J8's codex cell** (a live gateway probe on both served models, both
  roles, stream and non-stream, `data:` and `https:`, with the image-removed body as the positive
  control); and **A4's codex cell** (P3.175, `204892490`, 2026-08-28 — four configs over one fixture
  on the pinned `rust-v0.148.0`, `cat`/`grep -rn`/`grep -rln`/`ls` probes, with BOTH a no-profile
  control and a denies-an-unrelated-path control, the second of which is what discriminates *our deny
  line did it* from *the profile parent blocks every outside read*). **Five of the six inverted what
  they replaced**, which is the argument for the rig over the probe. **Six out of 263** is the honest
  score, and it is still the score to raise. **The vocabulary has no marker for this** — `ᵗ` is worn
  by a landed commit and by a rig alike — so behaviour-proof is tracked in prose here and nowhere
  else, which is a weakness of the vocabulary rather than of these six cells.
- **Not a priority list.** §Top of the queue is a recommendation; sequencing is the owner's.
- **Not stable against the tree.** Nine lanes were committing while this was assembled, and more
  landed between the build pass and the correction pass. **Six rows below were measured stale at

## Cell vocabulary

**Verdict** — five values, and the fifth is not the fourth:

| Verdict | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `covered` | The user can do it on this runtime. |
| `partial` | Some documented clauses hold, others do not. The row says which. |
| `absent` | The user cannot do it, and we know that. |
| `n/a` | Not this runtime's surface — the capability is meaningless here, with a reason. |
| `—` | **NO CLAIM.** Nobody measured it. Adopted from omnigent's frozen-record shape deliberately: a null is not an absence, and this ledger will not guess a cell to fill the grid. |
**A verdict scores the ROW, not the clause you measured** (RL1, 2026-09-12): a live drive that confirms one clause of a two-clause capability leaves `partial` standing — K34's catalogue reaches the picker and its label is still missing, and R1's `absent` for that reading would have said the user cannot do a thing they can. Write the clause into the Why; move the word only when the row's own sentence moves.


**Provenance** — the coverage map's existing marker vocabulary, plus one the codex distortion forces:

| Marker | Means | Strength |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ʳ` | **driven** — a live arm on the packaged build whose report names the controls | strongest: behaviour proven, not only landed (D1.85, 2026-09-17; the legend at the top carries the definition) |
| `ᵗ` | tracker row / plan row / landed commit is the evidence | strongest available here |
| `ʰ` | hand check — a call site, a schema, a shipped binary's strings, a file read | strong; still static |
| `ᵏ` | code probe only — identifier present or absent with a named positive control | **behaviour NOT proven.** This fork has shipped four fields that parsed and were never read |
| `ᵈ` | **doc-only** — the verdict rests on the vendor page and nothing in our tree or their binary was observed | weakest, and **now unused: 0 cells.** Its single instance (A5 codex) was refuted by measurement in P3.35. Kept in the vocabulary as the marker a future doc-derived cell must wear, and as the record that the one cell that wore it was **wrong** **Re-counted 2026-09-17: 32 cells (the top legend has the reading).** |
| `ˢ` | **propagated** — this cell repeats a verdict measured elsewhere (host-shared seam, or one runtime's measurement carried across). *A claim awaiting measurement* | not a measurement |

A propagated cell is visibly distinct from a measured one. That is the point: a survey of our
existing lists measured **46% of the Pi column as propagated rather than checked**, and that error
rate is the direct consequence of having eleven hand-maintained lists and nothing to derive from.

**Why absent** — the four reasons `runtime-capability-gaps.md` already defines, plus the fifth that
file itself uses:

| Reason | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `STRUCTURAL` | Follows from how the runtime or our integration is built. Changing it means changing the shape. |
| `DECISION` | An owner or engineering call with a recorded reason. Reversible — argue with the reason. |
| `PLANNED` | Has a row. The row is named. |
| `UNVERIFIED` | Believed from reading code or docs, never measured live. A claim, not a fact. |
| `DEFECT` | Built wrong or never built, with no decision behind it. `runtime-capability-gaps.md` uses this class for the Bash ceiling; the sweeps generate most of them. |

**Switch-safety** — half the owner's stated goal, and nothing tracked it before this column:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `UNIFORM` | Same on all three. No switch cost. |
| `REPORTED` | `runtimeSwitchCosts` or a post-switch notice tells the user. |
| `HONEST` | The capability itself degrades visibly and refuses to pretend. **The pattern to copy.** |
| `SILENT` | Behaviour changes across a switch with no diagnostic anywhere. |
| `SILENT-LOOSER` | Silent, **and in the security-loosening direction.** |
| `ADVERTISED` | **The anti-pattern.** The surface keeps offering what the target cannot do. |
| `HOST` | Host-level surface, runtime-independent. A switch changes nothing. |

**These seven are the whole vocabulary, and `plan-status.py` now says so out loud (P6.747, 2026-09-08).**
An eighth word invented in a cell used to fall through to `no-claim` in silence — `G2` said `NONE`
from `e8879beb1` until the P6.189 sweep noticed it by hand the same day, meaning *"no switch cost at
all"* and scored as *"nobody measured it"*, which is the opposite reading. It was caught by a reader,
not by the tool, and a reader is not a guard. The scorer warns by name whenever a Switch cell's first backticked token
is an ALL-CAPS word outside this table. **Before inventing a value, check whether one of the seven
already means it** — `NONE` was `UNIFORM`, spelled differently.

**`HOST` vs `UNIFORM`, written down because C3.45 had to choose between them
thirty times (2026-09-12).** The two both mean *a switch costs nothing*, and the
file had been using them interchangeably — B1 and B4 say `UNIFORM` about
host-owned capabilities while B7 says `HOST` about one. The rule those thirty
cells were derived under, so the next reader can re-derive rather than re-decide:
**`HOST` when the mechanism is a host surface no runtime participates in** (the
managed policy loader, the MCP pool gate, the updater, the output-style
composer — a switch changes which agent runs and not which code enforces);
**`UNIFORM` when the state is identical across the three for any other reason**,
which in family B is almost always a capability refused or absent on all three,
where there is nothing for a host to own. `HONEST` outranks both whenever the
three genuinely differ AND a surface says so — B9 and B31 are the two in that
family. All three score the Host column `covered`, which is correct for a column
that measures whether the SWITCH is safe rather than whether the capability
exists: a capability uniformly absent switches safely.

**OPEN QUESTION for the owner, raised 2026-09-11 by C3.62 (W16-i R10), recorded here because this is
where its answer belongs — no cell moves either way.** *Should a DECIDED REFUSAL be its own scorer
class, distinct from a defect and from `n/a`?* Measured at HEAD: `scripts/plan-status.py` defines
`HOST_CLASS = {'UNIFORM': 'covered', 'HOST': 'covered', 'HONEST': 'covered', …}` and its denominator
line is literally `denom = total - c['n/a']` (plus `denom = 4 * total - grand['n/a']` for the total
row), so **`n/a` and nothing else is subtracted**. There is no third word today, and both consequences
are real: a refusal written `n/a` RAISES the coverage number with nothing built, and a refusal written
`absent` counts against us as though it were unbuilt work — and this ledger is full of refusals. If
the answer is yes, it is one word in the table above plus one row in the scorer; if no, the ledger
keeps writing `absent` with `Why = DECISION` and the number stays deliberately pessimistic. It must
not be used to re-open the 2026-08-28 image decision.

## The two distortions you must carry into every reading

**1. Pi has no contract of its own — it is built to Claude's documentation.** So a Claude
capability absent on Pi is a gap *by definition*, and the Claude column does double duty: it is
both "what the SDK runtime does" and "the specification Pi is measured against". Two consequences
that bite: a `covered` in the Claude column can mean *the vendor's binary does it for us, and we
did nothing* (real for `isolation: worktree`, subagent budget caps, the stream watchdog, the whole
216-key settings cascade) — and a row where Pi is `absent` and Claude `covered` is often not a
missing feature but **an operator ceiling that exists on one runtime and not the other**, which is
worse than symmetric absence.

**2. The codex column is the weak one, and its weakness is not uniform.** Its map is 4 green out of
163 with **81 "not our surface" verdicts never re-triaged**, and the shipped `rust-v0.148.0` binary
has been measured **behaving opposite to its own documentation three times now**. A `ᵈ` cell would
be a verdict derived from the page alone, and **after P3.35 there are none**: the codex reader had
re-grounded nearly every doc-derived claim in a repo probe with a control, and the single exception
— A5 — turned out to be **refuted by a measurement committed in this file's own directory**.

**That refutation is the distortion, stated properly.** A5's whole proposition was a precedence rule
that exists nowhere but the page (*"Codex uses those older sandbox settings instead of
`default_permissions`"*), and the codex sweep's honest phrasing was *"the contract says we are wrong
and we have no evidence we are not."* The rig in `185172b05` supplied the evidence and **the page
is what was wrong**: the profile won on both axes, in both master-switch positions. So the working
rule for this column is not *"trust the page where we have nothing else"* — it is **"a codex cell
with no measurement behind it is a blank."** `github.com/openai/codex` is a reference here
**precisely because the page is not authority**, and the page is now marked *"Beta. Permission
profiles are under active development and may change."*

### C3.319 (2026-09-12) — the "55 unrunnable absence probes" is REFUTED, and the number that replaces it is FOUR

C3.266 swept the absence probes in these two files, ran the 11 it judged runnable, and named **55** as a
residue blocked by a shell metacharacter. That residue is the row C3.319 was born to close. Re-censused with
**the gate's own rule** — `unquotedShellMetachar` in `scripts/check-ledger-citations.ts`, which is the
function that actually decides whether a probe may be re-run — the two numbers do not agree, and the
difference is not a miscount:

| instrument | probes refused | what it is |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| the character class anywhere in the command, quotes ignored | **51** | the reading C3.266's 55 is consistent with |
| `unquotedShellMetachar`, the gate's own, quote-AWARE | **4** | the reading that decides runnability |

P6.933 made that function quote-aware precisely because the un-aware version *"was refusing the wrong 26"* —
eleven of them for a parenthesis inside a `:(glob)` pathspec, which is literal to every shell. So 47 of the
55 were never blocked: **inside single quotes nothing is special**, and a probe whose only metacharacter sits
there is runnable exactly as the prose spells it. The population itself is a reading with a date too: over
the two files a backticked `git grep …` span declaring a zero within 80 characters counts **99** (**90** if
the zero must be presented as the command's result), against C3.266's 66 — so quote the census, never a
number from it.

**The four the gate genuinely cannot run are repaired in their own cells rather than listed here**, each
re-spelled into a form with no pipe at all and each carrying a `**files=N**` the gate now re-runs: I23's
`--worktree` probe (ledger and twin, **refuted** — 3 files, one of them a reader), A41's permission-comment
probe (ledger and twin, **refuted** — the capability shipped, and the only file matching two of its three
names is a docblock quoting this ledger's own zero), and the out-of-scope spend-limit probe (**holds** at 0).
Two of the four were `-c` probes with no pathspec, which is the O21 defect a second and third time: a `-c`
probe prints one line per matching file, so a line-counting runner reads 1 whatever the tree holds.

**After the four repairs the gate-aware count is ZERO** — re-censused on the edited files, `unquotedShellMetachar`
refuses none of the 95 (86 by the strict reading), where the quote-unaware class still refuses 47.

### C3.249 (2026-09-12) — the measure-ahead sweep over all sixteen families, and it comes back NEGATIVE

QB7 stamped B6's Pi cell while its own applied sentence said the cell moves *only once* the absence was
written down with a positive control — a verdict applied ahead of its stated precondition. C3.249 asks
whether that happened anywhere else. **Method, so it can be re-run:** take every `kind: measure` item in
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-11-coverage-95-apply/<F>.json`, read each of its `ledger_edits` against the
cell at HEAD, and cross-reference the edited ROW against the ledger ids the coverage plan's 35 `C5` rows
name in their own task and note cells. **Population: 14 `measure` items of 144, carrying 43 ledger edits.**

| reading | count |
| --- | ---: |
| edits whose cell is at the JSON's `to` | 37 |
| edits differing from it only in the JSON's own spelling, or superseded by a later measurement | 5 |
| edits never applied | 1 |
| edited rows named by ANY of the 35 open `C5` rows | **1** (L65) |
| **cells stamped ahead of their measurement, other than the seed** | **0** |

**Nothing goes back to a pre-edit word, and the reason is not that the sweep was lenient.** Every other
`measure` item's edits rest on something already in hand rather than on the measurement the item schedules:
QA7's seventeen are marker upgrades onto a landed tripwire or refusals onto landed owner decisions, and its
`--restricted` measurement is gated on an SDK lift that has not happened; QA11's four and QF7's three and
QM11's two quote landed shas, with the scheduled rig re-deriving or proving a DIFFERENT row; QB8's three
rest on P6.250's refutation and its own note records why no re-run is owed; QG2's, QG3's two and QG11's
three leave the verdict where it was; QH13's two are the documented default on one runtime and a different
primitive on the other. QC5, QK4 and QK9 carry no ledger edit at all.

**The seed is confirmed and already recorded where it belongs.** B6's Pi cell says so in its own words —
*"the cell was stamped by the family-B apply BEFORE this control ran … a contingent stamp under the plan's
application rule 6. It happens to be right; the ordering was not."* — with C3.41's probe and its positive
control beside it. Reverting a cell whose precondition has since been satisfied would record a fact this
file has measured as false.

**Three by-products, each reported rather than swept.** (1) The ONE row the open `C5` set touches is L65,
and its claude arm is the opposite of this sweep's target: the JSON says `n/a ᵗ` and the cell reads
`absent ʰ`, because C3.189 REFUTED the `n/a` grounds by measurement and C5.28 is the open re-take — so the
JSON is the stale side, and an applier running it later would demote a correct cell and undo a refutation.
That is the third superseded apply-JSON entry found by a ledger lane, after QL3's L4/L39 and QM2's M33.
(2) G7's codex cell reads `partial ᵗ` where the JSON says `partial ʰ`: C3.84 drove the six arms on the
shipped `codex-app-server` and earned the marker, so the JSON is again the older side. (3) Four of the 43
edits write their verdict WITHOUT backticks (`n/a ʰ`, `covered ᵗ` ×3) where every cell in this file is
backticked, so a mechanical applier comparing strings reads them as mismatches — they are the whole of the
five-row "differs" line above, together with G7.

**What is NOT done here, with its measured reason.** Seventy-four of the strict census are runnable AND carry
no declaration (86 probes, 12 declaring a unit), so the gate does not re-run them: declaring them is
mechanical and is the right end state.
It is deliberately not done in this wave, because a `**files=N**` is a RATCHET, this tree has five lanes
committing to it, and AGENTS.md records a citation sweep losing that race nine times in forty minutes — a
sweep of seventy-five numbers taken mid-wave would hand the next reader a red gate whose findings are all
neighbours' commits. The cheap form is a single pass from a QUIET tree at close-out; the gate already reads
the INDEX rather than the working tree (`withCachedFlag`), so the only thing that can move a value under such
a pass is another lane's commit.

### C3.339 (2026-09-12) — that pass is RUN, and only 19 of the 55 could honestly be declared

The row above is the pass C3.319 deferred. **Its headline is that the mechanical sweep it describes does not
exist: most of the population cannot be declared without first deciding what its sentence means.**

**The instrument, so it can be re-run rather than re-counted.** Over the two files, every backticked span
starting `git grep ` or `grep ` that (a) presents a ZERO as the command's own result within 80 characters,
(b) is not a bare fragment naming the instrument rather than a command, and (c) carries no
`**files=N**`/`**lines=N**` inside the gate's own 40-character window. Runnability is not judged by hand: the
gate's own `unquotedShellMetachar`, `splitProbeArgv` and `listsFileNames` decide it, and the count is taken
the way `checkCountProbe` takes it — `git grep` with `--cached` prepended, the answer being the number of
non-empty OUTPUT lines, never the number a `-c` prints.

**Population at HEAD `dd1a8edd9`: 59 spans — 2 already declared, 2 refused by the gate's own metachar rule,
55 runnable and undeclared.** C3.319's reading of the same territory was 86 with 74 undeclared. **The two
numbers are not a contradiction and neither is a fact**: they are different instruments on a moving tree,
and the one above is stated in full precisely so the next reader re-runs it instead of quoting either.

**Of the 55, nineteen answer the zero their sentence claims, and those are now declared** — the declaration
REPLACES the stated result rather than sitting beside it, because two statements of one number are how the
two drift apart and only one of them is re-runnable. At zero the unit word cannot be wrong in either
direction (nothing matched, so nothing matched in 0 files AND on 0 lines), so a `files` written over a
command carrying no `-l` is corrected in passing without the claim moving — the P6.920 defect, retired
quietly where it is free to retire.

**Eleven more are `grep` rather than `git grep`, and NONE of them is declarable — by the gate's own rule,
not by this lane's judgement.** `checkCountProbe` runs exactly one shape of `grep`: `-c` over ONE literal
path, flag bundles of `a`/`c`/`i` only. Five distinct commands sit behind the eleven spans and every one of
them fails that: two carry no `-c` at all, one adds `E` to the bundle, one adds `o` and names two paths, and
one — the `maxTurns` probe — names NO PATH, which under AGENTS.md's §Traps means it reads STDIN and hangs a
runner rather than answering. A declaration on any of them would hand the gate a number it never re-runs,
which is the false comfort this row exists to remove.

**The remaining twenty-five answer something other than zero, and NOT ONE of them is simply a stale
absence.** Four mechanisms, each with a named example, because the fix differs per mechanism:

| mechanism | example | why the number is not a refutation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the prose scopes the command in WORDS the command does not carry | A43's three-name rules probe reads *"over packages/core/src and packages/shared/src/protocol"* while the command has no pathspec at all | it searched the whole tree, so the answer is not the sentence's question — C3.319's own class |
| the pattern is a REGEX the sentence reads as a literal | A19's `.codex/rules`, where the leading dot matches any character | the 41 it answers is not 41 hits on the string the sentence names |
| the command has no pathspec, so it counts the fork's OWN PROSE | the accessibility and colour-vision probes, two unrelated patterns both answering exactly 28 | these two documents are in the tree, and they contain the words |
| the zero is HISTORICAL and a re-run is already recorded in the same sentence | K15's `opusplan` (*"re-run 2026-09-08: 5 files"*), H39's `'--agents'` (*"re-run 2026-09-08: 1 hit"*) | the leading zero is a dated reading, not a live claim, and declaring it would pin history |

**The twenty-five, by the row that carries them**, so the next lane picks one up rather than re-censusing:
A19, A40, A43, H36, H39, H42, H51, K9, K15, L29, L51, plus five in prose sections rather than table rows
(the guardian count, the accessibility pair, the vim-mode probe and the workflow-stagger probe). Each needs
the judgement C3.319 spent on four of its own: re-spell the command to be the question the sentence asks,
or retire the sentence in words. **That is the honest residue of this row and it is deliberately not
guessed at here** — a number written beside a sentence it refutes is worse than no number at all.

## The switch-safety column's nine unmeasured cells — measured 2026-08-28

The owner's ruling: the runtime columns' 60 no-claims are blocked on someone else, but **the nine
switch cells were blocked on nobody** — the host is ours. They were measured in this wave rather
than deferred. **Six now carry a verdict; three stay `—`, and those three are the successful
outcome, not the failed one.**

| Row | Before | After | What settled it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `D1` | a correction, not a verdict | `HOST ʰ` | Both reporting channels are host-side and take no per-runtime input, so the under-reporting is uniform BY CONSTRUCTION. The self-reference is answered, not dodged. |
| `E2` | *"Not a switch issue"* | `HONEST ᵗ` | P3.32 (`fe26568f5`) shipped a user-visible refusal to pretend — **at one call site, claude's**. Scored as honest on the arm that has it, with the other two arms named as unmeasured. |
| `F3` | `—` | `ADVERTISED` **and** `HONEST ʰ` → **`HONEST ᵗ`** (x8) | Two layers disagreed: the dispatch seam refused `/subtask` by name on the runtimes that cannot fork (claimant set pinned to Pi by a biconditional test), while the composer menu offered it on all three. **`3f1248c16` closed the menu layer** with one table whose every row reads the predicate its own seam reads, so the `ADVERTISED` half is gone and the row is `HONEST` at both layers. |
| `J10` | prose declining to score | `SILENT ʰ` | The previous cell waited on the claude direction. Pi→codex is a switch too, and it is measurable: Pi executes web search, codex ships `web_search = "disabled"`, and no channel mentions the loss. |
| `L9` | `—` | `HOST ʰ` | The skill-disable a user actually meets is a four-state host-side override layer enforced on the BASE class, not codex's native file. |
| `L10` | `—` | `HOST ʰ` | One `SKILL_LISTING_MAX_CHARS` in the one `PromptBuilder` every backend consumes. The row's *"no cap at all"* is refuted; the true gap is that the cap is a flat constant rather than a share of the window. |
| `B8` | `—` | **`—`** | Our half is host-side and measured, but a HOST verdict would rest on the claude SDK's own managed-location skill discovery, never probed against a closed binary. |
| `E3` | `—` | **`—`** | The host reader is confirmed absent with a positive control, but the two deciding arms are vendor compaction inside runtimes we do not read. |
| `K4` | prose scoping the row | **`—`** | The subject exists on one connection type of one runtime, so there is no cross-runtime proposition for any value to be true of. Made an explicit null rather than left as prose. |

**Two by-products worth more than the cells that produced them.**

- **L9 and L10's codex cells were both scored against codex's NATIVE mechanism, and the capability
  the user meets is served host-side on every runtime.** L10's *"no cap at all"* is simply false at
  HEAD. Neither verdict was flipped by this pass — re-scoring a runtime column is not the switch
  lane's zone — but both row notes now carry the measurement, and both are re-score candidates.
  **L9 has since been re-scored (r8, 2026-08-28): all three cells read `covered ᵗ`.** Its evidence
  was re-derived at HEAD rather than taken from this note — four override states, three enforcement
  points, none provider-gated, one of them a private method on `BaseAgent`. **L10 is still a
  candidate and nobody has taken it**, which makes it the cheapest unclaimed correction left in this
  file: the same shape, one `SKILL_LISTING_MAX_CHARS` in the one `PromptBuilder` every backend
  consumes.
- **A near-miss that belongs in the trap register.** `git grep … | head` reported
  `buildClaudeContextWindowWarning` as having no non-test caller, which would have made P3.32's
  durable half a fifth field that parses and is never read. It has one — `packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts` symbol `startLocalAdapterRuntime` —
  and `head -10` had truncated it away, because the test file sorts before the source file. The
  repo's own rule (*"never `head -N` a grep before knowing the hit count"*) caught it on the re-run.
  **An absence probe with a `head` in it cannot fail.**

**How to read a switch cell mechanically:** the verdict is the cell's LEADING backticked token,
optionally bolded. Vocabulary words appearing later in a cell are prose — the null cells explain
which verdict they declined to write and why, so a scan that greps the whole cell will report
verdicts that are not there.

**The one live consumer got this wrong, and it is FIXED — this paragraph was itself stale, in the
exact shape it was written to warn about.** `scripts/plan-status.py`'s comment said *"take only the
first backticked token"* while `switch_verdict` iterated over **every** backticked token and returned
the first vocabulary hit anywhere in the cell, so `A5`'s `—` followed by the prose *"the previous
`SILENT-LOOSER` is refuted"* was booked as that verdict: **a cell saying a verdict was WITHDRAWN
counted as the verdict**, the precise inversion this column exists to prevent. It was caught by
counting rather than reading — the leading-token rule gave 55 rows in the script's `absent` class and
the script reported 56. **`4b45703df` fixed it**, and re-probed at HEAD `switch_verdict` now takes
`tokens[0]` and nothing else. **The fix landed BEFORE the r8 pass that left this text standing**, so
for one pass this file described a live defect in a script that had already been repaired — which is
the same failure as a stale `Why` column, one level up. The leading-token rule is now the contract in
both places, and the mechanical reading rule above is what a future consumer must implement.

# The ledger

Ordered by user-visible value: what stops a harmful action, then what an organisation can enforce,
then what leaves the machine, then whether a switch is honest, then everything else.

This section exists so that no cell below has to be taken on trust: every transformation rule is written here
rather than inferred from the result.

Separately, four admitted rows **describe the same capability as one of those six new ledger rows**. They were

**P6.748 (2026-09-08) ran that pass. It was four; it is SEVEN, and the four flagged ones are merged.**

| retired | merged into | flagged at admission? | how it was found |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `F20` | `F9` | yes | keyword |
| `J52` | `J12` | yes | keyword |
| `J53` | `J13` | **no** | provenance link + text similarity |
| `J54` | `J14` | yes | keyword |
| `J55` | `J15` | yes | keyword |
| `J56` | `J16` | **no** | provenance link |
| `O18` | `O3` | **no** | text similarity |

**Two instruments, and neither alone was enough.**

1. **The provenance link, which is the strongest and was sitting in the file the whole time.** Five of the six
   new ledger rows OPEN their `Why` cell with *"P6.358, denominator `J5x`"* — the sweep row they were written
   from. `J12`→`J52`, `J13`→`J53`, `J14`→`J54`, `J15`→`J55`, `J16`→`J56`. The admission's keyword search
   flagged three of those five. **A row that names its own source is a duplicate by construction**, and no
   similarity metric was needed to see it:
   ```sh
   grep -aoE 'denominator `?[A-Z][0-9]+`?' docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-capability-ledger.md | sort | uniq -c
   ```
2. **Text similarity, calibrated against the four KNOWN duplicates as a positive control** — which is what
   killed the first two instruments before they could report a clean answer. Stripping code spans (they look
   like noise) scored the known `J52` ↔ `J12` at **0.000**, because the only word the two share is
   `alwaysLoad`; plain cosine scored the known `J55` ↔ `J15` at **0.174**, because one text is three times
   longer than the other. The instrument that reaches **4 of 4** keeps code spans as high-idf tokens, scores
   containment-of-the-shorter beside cosine, and adds a shared-rare-token channel (df ≤ 5 of 631). It returns
   **556 candidate pairs out of 59 325**, every one of which was read; `O18` ↔ `O3` is the only duplicate in
   that list the provenance probe could not have found, and it announces itself in its own evidence cell
   (*"Ledger `O3` is STALE on all three cells; its DEFECT text is verbatim the pre-fix state"*).

**What the pass does NOT claim.** Recall is measured against four known positives, not against the truth: an
eighth duplicate whose two rows share neither a provenance line nor vocabulary would score below the cut and
was not read. The candidate list is reproducible from the two rules above, and a later reader who lowers the
cut is extending this pass rather than repeating it.

**A merged row is retired, not deleted.** The retired row keeps its position, its capability text and all of
its evidence; its id is struck (`~~J52~~`), its three verdict cells become `—`, and its `Why` cell opens with
`**RETIRED … → `J12`**`. A struck id no longer matches `plan-status.py`'s capability-id pattern, so the row
leaves the denominator — 638 → **631** — while staying exactly where a reader of that section looks for it.
`plan-status.py` counts and prints the retirements, so the drop is auditable from the same command that
reports the coverage.

**And since P6.776 that command also READS THE PROVENANCE LINKS BACK** — instrument 1 above is no longer a
one-off grep in a closed row's narrative but a guard in `plan-status.py` (`provenance_warnings`), run every
time the coverage is printed. Four defects warn by name: a live row citing a `denominator <id>` that is still
LIVE (the duplicate-by-construction shape `J13`/`J53` and `J16`/`J56` sat in from the admission until P6.748),
two different live rows citing one sweep row, a cite naming an id this file no longer contains, and a retired
row whose merge target is missing or itself retired. **A live row citing a RETIRED row is SILENT, deliberately:
that is the resolved state, and all seven surviving cites are of that shape** — warning on it would print seven
warnings on a correct file, and a rule that cries wolf is a rule people stop running.

**What the merge carried.** Six of the seven pairs agreed on all three verdicts, so only evidence moved. The
exceptions are worth naming: `J12`'s claude cell stays `partial ʰ` against the retired row's `covered ʰ`,
because P6.358 DROVE that clause and measured the claude pin INERT — a sweep's unmeasured reading does not
beat a measurement; and `J12`'s codex cell took the retired row's `ʰ` marker, because both cells said `n/a`
and only one of them claimed a hand check.

## A. The safety floor — what stops a harmful action

| # | Capability | Pi | Claude | Codex | Why absent | Switch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | Have a model-backed judge review high-risk actions (secret exfiltration, credential probing, destructive ops, protected-branch git) while in Allow-all | `partial ᵗ` | `n/a ᵗ` | `absent ᵗ` | DECISION — recorded, and the recorded word is *"not covered **yet**"*. Blocked on receipt/audit provenance for a second permission authority; the absence on claude is **pinned by a test**. **MEASURED 2026-08-28, and the measurement makes the claude cell WORSE than *"we have not built ours yet"* — P3.93 / P3.96 (`b0e6f0044`).** The vendor ships its own judge, we already enable it, and it is consulted **zero times**: in auto mode the SDK classifier IS the permission prompt, and our PreToolUse hook returns `allow`, which skips the prompt. Five arms, two controls, env scrubbed of every `CLAUDE*`/`ANTHROPIC*` key, classifier requests counted off our own loopback upstream — `auto` with no hook (positive control) → **2 classifier requests**; **`auto` + our shipped `allow`, WHAT WE SHIP → 0 classifier requests, 0 `canUseTool`, and `curl … \| sh` EXECUTED WITH NO REVIEW**; a hook with no `permissionDecision` → 2 requests, denied fail-closed. The binary’s own log string is `bypassing permission prompt`. **A bare hook `ask` is NOT the repair** — it never reaches the classifier, it raises a real prompt; the documented *"the classifier can still deny"* holds only on the `hookAskFloor` path, which needs an ask **rule** as well. P3.96 also inverted its own premise: the availability gate is a **DENY list**, so `tgpt/qwen35-397b-a17b-fp8` reports `supportsAutoMode: true` and this mechanism is live on the shipped default card. **And the blocker on the fix is now a decision rather than an unknown — P3.121 (`6f3cc6443`): the gateway answers the classifier’s prompt in the shape the binary parses, 28 of 28** (25 hops across 13 end-to-end turns plus 3 replays), denying an unnamed `curl … \| sh` and running the same command when the user names the source; cost one or two hops of ~24.2k input tokens each, 2.1–30.6 s added latency (median 7.5 s), absent from `modelUsage`. **NEITHER commit is a fix and this cell did not move.** What moved is that the absence is measured instead of assumed, and the open decision is now latency and variance rather than feasibility. **THREE MORE COMMITS LANDED IN THIS FAMILY 2026-08-28 AND THE CELL STILL DID NOT MOVE — read that as the row, not as an oversight (s2).** **P3.94 + P3.95 (`ecddf100a` + `c89436679`)** now hand the classifier a policy describing THIS deployment instead of letting it judge a T-Bank install against Anthropic's generic defaults: `environment` names three hosts unrecognised to those defaults (the Nestor gateway from `auth/nestor.ts`, emitted only when the adapter resolved that upstream; the GitLab host from `git remote -v`; the Artifactory host from `bunfig.toml` — without them an ordinary `bun install` or `git push` reads as escalation), one `hard_deny` on **disclosure** of the gateway JWT (chosen because P3.147's mirror covers Read/Edit/Write, was measured NOT to cover search results, and **does not cover `Bash` at all**, which is the band the classifier judges), one `soft_deny` on deleting the same file (it also signs the user out of nessy-cli, which is unguessable from the path), and **`allow` deliberately EMPTY and pinned by a test** — an allow can only widen. The `"$defaults"` splice was **asserted rather than inferred**: containment, zero built-in lines dropped, ours landing immediately after the built-in entries of the same section — and that assertion caught a bug in its own first version. P3.95 settled the blocker: `sdk.mjs` gates the `autoMode` schema OFF with an empty shape while the shipped binary gates it ON with the full four-array schema, and **the disagreement is INERT** because the JS gate feeds the JS layer's own settings-FILE reader and is never applied to `Options.settings`; The SDK's own file-checkpointing API is in the bundle we ship (`rewindFiles` ×3) with zero call sites, and its hard precondition `extraArgs: { 'replay-user-messages': null }` is passed nowhere. **RESIDUE RECORDED 2026-09-07 (P6.610), and the premise it was born with is HALF-REFUTED — worth reading before anyone re-opens it.** P6.268 (`895c117e1` + `e443e83b4`, locale keys `369fc424f`) made a rewind name what it could not cover, with two categories — unwatched shell commands and background subagents — and deliberately WITHOUT a third for EXTERNAL edits. The reason recorded at the site was *"no signal in the transcript can distinguish them from a file nobody touched"* (`apps/electron/src/renderer/utils/rewind-report.ts:68-73`). **A signal does exist, on claude, and it is documented, typed and vendored:** `FileChanged` is in the shipped SDK’s `HOOK_EVENTS` and typed as `FileChangedHookInput` carrying `file_path` and `event` of `change`/`add`/`unlink` (`node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:644-652`), and `hooks.md#filechanged` says verbatim: *"Claude Code detects changes with a filesystem watcher, not by inspecting tool calls, so it runs the hook no matter what changed the file: an `Edit` or `Write` tool call, a script Claude runs with `Bash`, or a process outside Claude Code entirely."* **So the correct structural claim is not "no signal" — it is "no ORIGIN", and the page states the non-attribution as a DESIGN PROPERTY rather than an omission.** The one mechanism that sees an outside writer sees the model’s own writes identically, which is precisely the discrimination a rewind category needs. Two further bounds make it unusable for this even if origin were carried: it is WATCH-LIST scoped — *"Claude Code starts the watcher only when something names a file to watch"*, seeded from literal filenames or a dynamic `watchPaths` — so it cannot cover the arbitrary file set a rewind span touches; and it has **no decision control**. **The other two runtimes make the name actively misleading, which is the trap for the next reader.** On Pi the same event name means the OPPOSITE: `packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts` SYNTHESIZES `FileChanged` from the model’s own mutating tool calls, correlating the path across `tool_execution_start`/`_end` and probing existence beforehand to split `add` from `change` — so on Pi it can only ever report an edit the session made. On codex the nearest spelling is not a watcher at all: `fileChange` in `packages/codex-protocol/generated/v2` is the model’s own patch application (`ThreadItem` `"type": "fileChange"`, `FileChangePatchUpdatedNotification`, `FileChangeRequestApprovalParams`). **And the host already carries the inventory that says all this — read it before re-deriving any of the above.** `runtime-hook-events.ts` scores `FileChanged` `emitted` on the claude native route (*"the shipped binary constructs `hook_event_name:\"FileChanged\"` at one site that awaits the hook runner"*), `emitted` on Pi through `lifecycle-bridge.ts`’s `tool_execution_end` for a tool in `FILE_MUTATING_TOOLS` that did not error — with **`unlink` unreachable under that trigger, and the handler saying so** — and `UNMEASURED_LIFECYCLE` in `CODEX_HOOK_EVENT_EMISSION`. The consequence is recorded on the host too: `BaseAgent._hookWatchPaths` holds `SessionStart`’s `watchPaths` **INERT** by a decision that names this exact reason — *"Nessy’s `FileChanged` fires when a file-mutating tool completes rather than from a disk watcher, so there is no watch list to configure"* (`packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts` symbol `FileChanged`, citing `plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-b.md:329-331`). So one event NAME already means two different triggers across a switch, which is a second reason a rewind category built on it would not be uniform. **Verdict: STRUCTURAL, and the third category stays unbuilt on purpose** — asserting it without evidence would make the two honest categories read as boilerplate, which is the failure this row exists to avoid. ## G. Hooks and automation

| # | Capability | Pi | Claude | Codex | Why absent | Switch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| G1 | Have a hook event fire at all — SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, Notification, PreCompact/PostCompact and more | `covered ʰ` | `partial ʳ` | `partial ᵗ` | DEFECT — 50 emit sites, every one inside a Pi-named path. Claude's column is MEASURED, not empty: `MEASURED_HOOK_EVENT_COLUMNS` (`packages/shared/src/automations/runtime-hook-events.ts`) reads `anthropic: true` since P6.89 (`b3d569a06`, 2026-09-05), and the surviving residue is that every `emitted` verdict there cites the SDK's declared `HookEvent` union rather than an observed firing (`D1.16`). *(Corrected 2026-09-11 by C3.80 / W16-i R15: the sentence this replaces claimed twelve documented events had no Nessy-side emitter on claude, and P6.89 had refuted it five days before the follow-up plan was drafted.)* Codex emits exactly four and **discards the Stop hook's whole result, `decision: block` included.** **A narrower claude fact, measured 2026-08-28 and worse than the count above (s2): `buildSdkHooks()` has exactly ONE production consumer (`claude-agent.ts`) and `mergeClaudeSdkHooks` DROPS EVERY NON-INTERNAL `PreToolUse` MATCHER before it reaches the SDK** — so on claude a user's or a plugin's `PreToolUse` hook has no live reader at all, independently of whether the event is emitted (P3.176, `df9dd5135`). The same commit made the translator correct for the day it does have one: `block`/`deny` now leave through `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` + `permissionDecisionReason` instead of the pair `hooks.md` deprecates for this event; `ask` **travels at all** — strictly restrictive, and the direct pipeline already honoured it, so the two paths now agree; and `defer` gained a representation **two layers deep**, because `mergePreToolUseDecisionObjects`'s inline `rank()` omitted it entirely and scored it 0, **below `allow`**, so under the strict policy a later allow erased it before the translator was ever reached (the page's precedence is `deny` > `defer` > `ask` > `allow`, and the sibling native merge has always had it right — two functions doing one job, one correct). `allow` was deliberately NOT landed: it maps to omitting the field, which is P3.93's arm A4, the shape measured to silence the SDK classifier completely. P3.177 (`df9dd5135`) landed first so the union stopped declaring `'allow' \| 'ask' \| 'deny'` against the bundle's `'approve' \| 'block'` (the page is narrower still: *"The only value for `decision` is `"block"`"*). **The cell keeps `ʰ` rather than moving to `ᵗ`:** the commit measured the matcher drop, not the twelve-event count the `ʰ` rests on. **TWO DEFER DEFECTS CLOSED AND THE DOCUMENTED ORDERING RESTORED, 2026-08-31/09-01, and none of them moves the twelve-event count this cell's `ʰ` rests on.** (1) P3.124 (`31362b870`) measured the residue P3.176 left behind: `runClaudePreToolUseHookPipeline` narrowed the host decision union to `'allow' \| 'ask'` one hop before the payload was built, so a `defer` from a user, project or plugin hook fell into the empty branch and `buildClaudePreToolUseContinue`, seeing no decision at all, named **`allow`** — the strongest non-terminal value arriving as the one value it can never lose to, with the payload additionally telling the runtime to skip its own prompt. (2) `5249afe2f` closed it as a stated POSTURE rather than by emitting `defer`: the runtime CAN defer (`hooks.md#defer-a-tool-call-for-later` names this exact surface — *"an Agent SDK app or a custom UI built on top of Claude Code"* — and the SDK types both halves), but the HOST cannot receive it, because the claude event adapter reads no `terminal_reason: 'tool_deferred'` and fills no `deferredToolUse`, so a real deferral would end the turn with the tool unrun and nothing on screen saying why. At `1c02fa3b3` `SessionManager.admitAgentMessage` (`:4079`) resolves an inbound mode, releases anything held, and calls `admitCrossSessionMessage` with the sender, a hash of the text, a clock and the receiver's current queue depth. The numbers are the page's, not invented — `CROSS_SESSION_QUEUE_CAP = 50` (*"queues at most 50 accepted messages for Claude to read"*) and `CROSS_SESSION_HOLD_CAP = 100` (*"holds at most 100 messages … and past that drops the oldest"*) — while the **rate limit is undocumented and was therefore chosen against the system's RESTING behaviour rather than against zero**: one message per sender per receiver TURN is resting, so ten per minute sits an order of magnitude above any legitimate coordinator and still catches a runaway exchange bounded by tool dispatch. **And the sender is TOLD, which the page requires explicitly:** `CrossSessionVerdict` carries `delivered \| held \| refused \| dropped` with the guard named (`rate-limit \| identical-repeat \| queue-cap`), and `send_agent_message` reports anything but `delivered` as a **failed** send carrying the receiver's own note — never as a success the model would then wait on a reply for. ## P. The board, tasks, planning, projects and pages (1.42.0, UA plan)

Admitted 2026-10-03 by UA10.1 (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-23-upstream-adoption-0-13-4-board-planning-pages.md`): ten rows, one per shipped surface of the upstream-adoption plan — the kanban board, durable tasks, the Conductor, Generate, projects, the project context layer, the page tools, page isolation, refresh and actions, publishing. Every capability is host-provided through the session-tools seam, so the three runtime cells are UNIFORM by construction where the tool set is; where a runtime cannot carry a piece, the cell says so and cites the deviation. Verdicts cite the owning UA row; a row's control is named in its Why cell.

## Q. Permission keys, sources, the decision model and the 0.15.1 delta (1.42.0 security fixes and 1.43.0, UB plan)

Admitted 2026-10-17 by UB10.1 (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-14-upstream-adoption-0-15-1.md`) on the PROVISIONAL ship list: twenty-two rows. Four are the 1.42.0 security fixes the 1.43.0 plan points at (the remember key, the argv inspectors, the domain grant, source activation); each cites its UA12 row, because all four landed and shipped in 1.42.0. Eleven are the decision model: the core unit, then one row per landed feature row. One is rtk. Six are the 0.15.1 delta capabilities: append-only project memory, the MCP prompt tools, `_intent` on source calls, one sign-in for parallel sessions, browser passwords out of transcripts, and Stop ending only the reply. **What "provisional" means here, stated because the plan row's wording and the tree's state differ:** the row reads the ship list as the rows whose live cases have PASSED when it runs, and on 2026-10-17 no 1.43.0 case has been driven — every drive is owed to the END sitting. These rows are therefore admitted from LANDED code with the live PASS owed, the shape section P was admitted in, and UB11.1 removes, in its own commit, the row of anything it holds out. **The ten decision-model feature rows (Q6–Q15) carry a stronger caveat:** under the plan's one rule for Phase 6 feature rows a feature ships only on a live PASS with a decision provider the controller may use, and OQ-43.13's default (d) names none. Unless the owner names a provider before the sitting, UB11.1 removes all ten, and each says so in its Why. # Where the sources disagreed

A disagreement between two of our own artefacts is a finding, not noise. Five, with my verdict.

**D1 — The guardian is not on the switch surface (claude sweep) vs it is (`runtime-capability-gaps.md`).**
The claude sweep's row A1 says: *"`runtime-switch-costs.ts` — the module built to enumerate switch
costs — has zero guardian references (`git grep -ci guardian` → 0; control `runPreToolUseChecks`
→ 3 in the same file)."* `runtime-capability-gaps.md` says P2.315 added a `guardianJudge` row
**between the first two**, re-measured 2026-08-28 by *running* `runtimeSwitchCosts` rather than
re-reading the paragraph. **I measured it (2026-09-05): guardian `lines=11`, control `runPreToolUseChecks` `lines=2`; RE-MEASURED 2026-09-08 (W9-bn) with `git show HEAD:<file> | grep -c -i guardian` → `lines=32` and `grep -c runPreToolUseChecks` → `lines=5`, in
`apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/runtime-switch-costs.ts` at HEAD.**
**RE-DERIVED WITH ITS PATHSPEC 2026-09-12 (C3.266 / W17-b's proposed row 2, W17-c):** the sweep's own
spelling `git grep -ci guardian` carries NO pathspec, so as written it reads the whole tree and its `0`
is not a reading of what this sentence claims — and a `-c` probe prints one line per matching file, so a
runner counting output lines cannot read it at all. Re-stated over the file the sentence IS about and run
today: `git grep -a -i guardian -- apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/runtime-switch-costs.ts` → **lines>=33**,
positive control `git grep -a -F runPreToolUseChecks -- apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/runtime-switch-costs.ts` → **lines>=8**.
The FLOOR form is deliberate and is the reason this repair is gate-checkable at all: both numbers count
matches inside a LIVE source file that grows on most commits to it, so the claim is *non-zero, and here
is what the hits are*, never the exact value. Both earlier readings are kept above with their dates; this
is the fourth in the series (0 → 11 → 32 → 33) and the verdict it supports has not changed since C1 below
corrected it. Both of
the sweep's numbers moved, so it measured a different tree or a different path. **Verdict: the
gaps document is right and the sweep's switch-safety sentence — *"the only place a user is told is
a Settings sub-page"* — is refuted at HEAD.** The capability verdict (`absent` on claude and codex)
is unaffected; only the "silently" is. This matters because A1 was the sweep's nominated worst case
*on the strength of that silence*.

**D2 — Agent-declared hooks on claude: one gate and cheap (sweep) vs a refused design (gaps doc).**
The sweep reads the inline justification at the gate, finds it unsound on this fork (the SDK never
sees the SKILL.md whose frontmatter carries the hooks, because we pass `plugins: []`, ban the
`Skill` tool, and materialize no skills tree), and concludes *"one gate; the layer already exists."*
`runtime-capability-gaps.md` records a DECISION with a different and stronger argument: we hold
**Nessy's normalized automations config, not the author's block** — a status message is gone, a
timeout has changed units, `if`/`async`/`once` are stripped by name — so rebuilding it would run a
command the author never wrote or fail the CLI's all-or-nothing parse and delete every agent in the
session; refusing the agent was rejected too, because every other runtime admits it. **Verdict:
both are true of different things.** *Skill-frontmatter* hooks are the sweep's cheap gate;
*agent-declared* hooks are the gaps doc's refused rebuild. The ledger scores them as one row (G3)
with the reason `DECISION`, because the expensive half governs.

**D3 — Does our system prompt reach codex?** The codex reader: *"Our system prompt does not reach
codex at all"* (the config's top-level `instructions` key is one of 42 unwritten scalars). The
claude reader, on the output-style row: `systemPrompt` hits `packages/shared/src/agent/codex-agent.ts` symbol `createRuntime`, and codex calls
`buildContextParts` → `buildVolatileContextParts`. `runtime-capability-gaps.md` reconciles them:
*"We write no system prompt — not a limit… Our context blocks ride the user message"* (STRUCTURAL,
because `thread/inject_items` writes permanent rollout records and the cached-prefix option kills
prompt-cache reuse). **Verdict: `partial`.** Our guidance reaches codex through the user turn; the
instruction *channel* is unused; and the specific thing that was never injected either way is the
prompt-injection guidance (A3).

**D4 — Where the managed-capability gate lives. RESOLVED by P3.35 — and the disagreement was
between this file and the tree, not between two sources.** The claude sweep pinned the early return
at `storage-runtime.ts:806` with `isPiCapabilityTurn`; at HEAD it reads `:842` with
`isRuntimeCapabilityTurn`. That was not "an in-flight commit" to re-measure later: it is **P2.314
(`acb727ae8`), closed**, and the answer to its own first question is the load-bearing part — *the
gate was NOT deliberate.* It was a per-provider early return standing where a host-side filter
belongs, so the managed MCP and plugin lists lapsed on every runtime but Pi; it now reads
`provider !== undefined`, browse stays unnarrowed on purpose, and because the answer was "not
deliberate" **nothing was owed to `runtime-capability-gaps.md`** — that destination was conditional
on the opposite finding. **B1 claude and B2 claude gained a verdict rather than losing coordinates,
and B1's Pi cell lost one**, for the residual P2.368. The carve-out that was "under active
investigation" is A12: reproduced, fixed (`3353e3215`), and now scored `partial` on all three.

**D5 — The coverage maps against both sweeps.** The sweeps corrected the maps in **both**
directions, repeatedly, and this is the strongest argument for deriving per-runtime sets from one
record rather than maintaining eleven lists: `isolation: worktree` on claude was 🟥 and is covered
(H7); managed app updates was 🟥 and is built (B7); worktree setup scripts was 🟥 and is built (I5);
the advisor was recorded as "0 files" and is 78 (H3); managed MCP and gateway headers were credited
green and are unreachable on claude (B1, M2); a model retirement was probed as harmless at 0 files
and is 6 (K4). The claude sweep separately counted **41 wrong coverage-map cells**. I did not turn

# Corrections I measured myself

**C1-C2 are from the build pass; C3-C6 from the P3.35 correction pass.** Every one is a row that
arrived stale, re-measured at HEAD with a named positive control.

**C1 — The guardian IS on the switch surface.** See D1.
`git grep -a -c -i guardian -- apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/runtime-switch-costs.ts`
→ **11**; positive control `runPreToolUseChecks` on the same file and command → **2**. The reader
reported 0 and 3. Row A1's switch-safety corrected from `SILENT` to `REPORTED`.
**RE-RUN 2026-09-12 (C3.266, W17-c) on the same file, in a form the citation gate can actually read:**
`git grep -a -i guardian -- apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/runtime-switch-costs.ts` → **lines>=33**,
positive control `git grep -a -F runPreToolUseChecks -- apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/runtime-switch-costs.ts` → **lines>=8**.
**The `-c` above is kept as written because it is the historical reading, and it is also the reason this
re-run drops the flag:** the gate re-runs a declared probe and counts its OUTPUT LINES, so a `-c` form
answers **1** whatever the file holds — measured, by declaring the `-c` form first and watching the gate
report 1 against a floor of 33 four times. That is AGENTS.md's own `-c` trap arriving inside the
instrument built to catch stale numbers, so a `lines=` declaration must use a form that prints one line
per match. The correction stands and only its numbers were a reading with a date — the file has kept
growing (43 switch-cost rows at HEAD, and W17-a's three-way judge paragraph landed in the `guardianJudge`
docblock as `f9d3170d6`), which is why this declaration names its pathspec and its instrument rather than
leaving a bare number for the next reader to inherit.

**C2 — The Pi Bash *timeout* ceiling has landed; the *output* ceiling has not.**
`git grep -al -F 'BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS' -- packages apps` → **files=7** (7 on 2026-09-24: `claude-agent.ts` joined with F1.528's own-turn bound comment, `f76861bec`, which names the CLI's ceiling by the same name — controller re-pin; re-run 2026-09-08, W9-bn; **4 files** when written), including
`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts`, `pi-harness/process-supervisor-port.ts` and a dedicated
`__tests__/pi-bash-timeout-ceiling.test.ts`; negative control (an invented name in the same file)
→ 0. The reader and `runtime-capability-gaps.md` both record Pi as having **no** operator ceiling.
That is stale. `BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` → **1 file, a test**, so the output half stands absent, as
the gaps document independently predicted (*"a knob gap, not a ceiling gap"* — Pi caps at a
hard-coded 64 KiB). Row J1 scored `partial` on Pi rather than `absent`.

**C3 — the codex credential deny is enforced, and the page is the thing that is wrong.** The rig in
`2026-08-28-codex-sandbox-enforcement.md` (`185172b05`) drove `command/exec` under three arms with
an isolated `CODEX_HOME` each. Shipped default (master switch OFF, deny emitted): reading
`credentials.enc` **refused**. Control (`off_true`, no profile emitted): **secret read**. Master
switch ON: refused. **The "off" column and the "on" column are identical on every row measured.**
A5 corrected `absent ᵈ` → `covered ᵗ`, its switch verdict withdrawn, and this file's `ᵈ` count
went to zero. The residual is that file's §4: a rejected `extends` fails **open** to stderr and the
session still looks sandboxed.

**C4 — our own floors reach codex; the ledger said they could not.** P2.140 (`bd12361a9`) extracted
`findNonNegotiableFloors` into `core/pre-tool-use.ts`; `codex-agent.ts` calls it at `:2101` and
`:3549`. Probed at HEAD on this branch: 2 live call sites, and `runPreToolUseChecks` in that file
still **0** with positive controls pi 10 / claude 2 — so the row is `partial`, not `covered`, and
the ledger's `absent` was stale by two days. Before the fix, driven on the production path: `rm -rf
~` with an ordinary `allow: ['Bash(rm:*)']` returned `{decision:'accept'}` **with no card**.

**C5 — the `ultracode` advertisement is closed in two of its three routes.**
`WORKFLOW_KEYWORD_DISPATCH_RUNTIMES` exists at HEAD in
`packages/shared/src/workflows/workflow-keyword.ts` as `Readonly<Record<AgentProvider, boolean>>`,
`pi: true` with the other three `false`, and it is the **only** consumer path
(`detectWorkflowKeywordTrigger`, one non-test caller at `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts` symbol `detectWorkflowKeywordTrigger`). That is
precisely the fix this file recommended as its cheapest structural repair — **it had already landed**
(P2.315, `d144ce041`) before the recommendation was written. What survives is the **menu row**,
open as P2.279.

**C6 — Pi does read `.claude/settings.json`.** `skill-overrides.ts` reads both `settings.json` and
`settings.local.json` through `readClaudeSettingsSkillOverrides` and merges them into the scope
layers; `permissions-config.ts` handles the same files' allow/ask/deny blocks; neither is gated on a
provider, and `claude-settings-store.ts` and `agent/memory/instruction-excludes.ts` share the parser.
Separately P2.313 (`3e66f5fbb`) measured `buildPiSubprocessEnv` **already spreading `process.env`**
(Pi 69 keys, claude 70, host 67, carrying `BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` and an invented control identically)
— so both the ledger's absolute *and* the fix everyone would reach for are wrong. L1 Pi → `partial`.

**What C2 means for anyone reading this file later:** it was written during nine concurrent lanes.
A row's *capability* verdict is more durable than its *file:line*, and both are more durable than
its "cheap / one line" costing. **Re-measure any row before you queue it**, with a positive control
on the same run — six mechanisms on this branch return a confident wrong answer, and the one that
bit hardest here was a probe that was simply older than the tree.
