# Top of the queue

Five, ordered by *how soon this bites a real user*, not by fix size. Each names what it costs and
what must be measured before it is touched.

**Corrected by P3.35 — this list was the part of the file most damaged by not having read the
plan.** Item 5 was **already fixed** two routes out of three before it was written; item 1 already
had an open row (P2.252) and got a duplicate (P3.30); and the item held *out* of the list for
needing "one live turn" — A5 — had already had that turn run and committed. **Two of five queue
entries were archaeology, and the excluded one was the closest thing in the file to a result.** Read
the plan's tracker before queueing anything from here.

**1. ~~`CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE` is never set~~ — DONE, and this item was wrong twice (struck 2026-08-28).**
Row **C1** records it **FIXED by P3.30** (`687ecff05` + `0cac5b635`); this paragraph and that row have
contradicted each other since, and both predate the `9e0596f2e` baseline, so the ledger refresh left
them alone and reported the clash instead. The second error is this item's own framing: it called C1
*"the only row whose failure the user experiences as the product is broken"*, and that is **refuted by
measurement** — codex's model route is **loopback plain HTTP by construction**, so the default turn was
never broken; what was broken is codex's own TLS egress, which is narrower. Kept rather than deleted
because the reasoning it carried is instructive: the fix hands a third-party binary our trust material,
and P3.30 measured that `CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE` **outranks** `SSL_CERT_FILE` inside one bundle — so
writing ours unconditionally would overwrite an operator's. Still true and still worth sequencing with
**J11**: both are codex reaching the network, and a session that cannot resolve DNS will not notice a CA.

**2. Rewind reports success and restores no files on two of three runtimes (F1).** The same button,
the same success toast, two different truths — the one shape in this ledger where the product
actively tells the user something false about their working tree. The SDK's own file-checkpointing
API is in the bundle we already ship with zero call sites. Measure first: whether
`enableFileCheckpointing` works without the `replay-user-messages` extra arg, which is its
documented hard precondition and is passed nowhere.

**3. Auto-compaction silently does not happen on the default-on gateway card (E2).** A session was
measured carried to 227,337 tokens with no compaction, no boundary and no error, on the card most
users are on, for any gateway model missing a `contextWindow` — and our own fetcher keeps a
hard-coded window table *because the gateway omits that field*. This is a live defect, not a parity
gap. Measure first: which shipped gateway ids are absent from that table today.

**4. The three security defences that vanish on a runtime switch — now one and a half, not three
(A1 + A2 + A3).** **A3 is DONE** (`0cac5b635`, landed while this file was being corrected): the host
safety guidance rides codex's `developerInstructions` at all three thread-creating call sites. **A2
is half done and this file said it was structural** — P2.140 (`bd12361a9`) extracted our
non-negotiable floors and codex calls the same function, so a `rm -rf ~` cleared by an ordinary
allow rule now refuses; what does not run there is the rest of the pipeline. **A1 alone remains**,
and it is blocked rather than unwritten: the guardian judge port is `provider === 'pi'` by
construction, so the consult cannot reach claude or codex without new host infrastructure — recorded
as deviation **Dev-23**, with the cost table now naming the Guardian (correction C1). The queue item
is no longer "three defences": it is **A1's infrastructure decision**, plus P2.197's bounded
exception on codex, where six of seven modes emit `on-request` and a command the model never raises
reaches no gate.

**s2, 2026-08-28 — A1 got THREE commits and stayed `absent`, and the queue item is now sharper, not
larger.** The vendor's own judge is enabled, is now told what deployment it is judging (P3.94/P3.95,
`ecddf100a` + `c89436679`), has its hop sequence pinned against a vendor bump (P3.140, `d0ff6b250`)
and has a typed refusal receipt waiting for it (P3.97, `233b192e7`) — **and it is still consulted on
approximately nothing**, because our own PreToolUse returns `allow` on every path and in auto mode
the prompt IS the classifier. So A1 is no longer *"blocked on host infrastructure"* alone: on claude
there is a second, native authority that is **fully configured and switched off by one line of ours**,
and turning it on is an OWNER decision about latency (median 7.5 s), cost (~24.2k input tokens a hop,
invisible in `modelUsage`) and verdict variance — P3.139, open. **That is the native-first rule's own
shape**: the runtime already has the mechanism, we already enable it, and what remains is neither
building nor porting but deciding. Note also what P3.176 (`df9dd5135`) bounded while landing next
door: `defer` — the one hook shape that lets the classifier run — now exists at both layers, and the
translator carrying it has **no live reader**, so the decision cannot be reached by accident.

**5. ~~The `ultracode` keyword hands a claude session a directive naming a tool it does not have~~
— WITHDRAWN, it was fixed before this was written. What is left is the menu row (H2, P2.279).**
The `Record<AgentProvider, boolean>` this entry recommended **exists**:
`WORKFLOW_KEYWORD_DISPATCH_RUNTIMES`, landed in P2.315 (`d144ce041`), and the slash-command route
was gated earlier still by `BaseAgent.canDispatchWorkflowCommands()` (P2.212). What it did **not**
close is the third route the entry claimed it would: `/workflow-name` is **still listed in the menu**
on claude and codex, so the user is offered a command that now refuses — open as P2.279, blocked
only by zoning, in `SessionManager`. **The lesson is worth more than the row:** this file costed a
fix at "one table" for three symptoms, and the table turned out to close two and to have landed
already. A cost written without reading the tracker is a guess. The pattern to copy is still H1 —
the review skill that refuses to pretend a review ran — and P2.279 is the last route where this
product still pretends.

**Promoted in their place, both from artefacts this file had not read.**

**6. The codex agent's shell has no network in any shipped configuration (J11).** `npm install`,
`git fetch`, `curl` — all unreachable, measured against a control column that returned `200` and
`301`, and **DNS fails by exiting 0 with empty output**, so the user is told *no such host* rather
than *denied*. It is `OQ-11` in the plan, awaiting an owner call between three costed options.
Nothing to measure first; the measurement is committed.

**7. A denied MCP server can still spawn with its credentials (A12, second instance).** The first
instance was reproduced (pid 15010, writing its own configured environment) and fixed in
`3353e3215`. **P2.368 is the second**: built-in dp MCP records are appended *after* the managed
filter and escape the denylist on every path including runtime turns — measured surviving a Pi turn
while denied by both name and command. It fires only where an administrator enabled a dp server, and
those are the servers wired to our gateway credentials. ~two lines, in the file the sibling just
touched.

**What was deliberately not in the top five, and what happened to it.** Both exclusions were wrong,
and both for the same reason.

- **A5** was held out as *"doc-only… needs one live turn before anyone chooses a direction. Run the
  probe; then it is number one."* **The probe had already been run and committed** — same day, same
  directory, `185172b05` — and it did not merely resolve the row: it **inverted** it. The deny is
  enforced, and the sweep's recommended fix would have **removed a working security control.** The
  live turn this file asked for is the reason A5 is now the strongest cell in the grid.
- **K4** was held out as *"three days on the clock… excluded only because it does not touch the
  default gateway connection."* It was **closed with three days to spare** (P2.309, `e3f0a485c`),
  with the replacement verified present in the shipped catalogue rather than trusted from the page,
  and a warning that makes the next silent degradation loud. Its neighbour is still open: P2.318 —
  the *main* codex preference list is one-of-seven live, and that one is an owner call because it
  changes which model a connection talks to.

**The generalisation, since it cost this file two of its seven judgements:** an exclusion reasoned
*"someone must measure X first"* is only sound if you have checked that nobody already did. Both of
these had been measured, in artefacts a directory listing would have shown.
